definition: the highest point; ideal or culminating example
memoryTip: Apo-theos: raised to godlike status—the peak or ideal.
correctPassage: The performance was widely seen as the apotheosis of her career.
wrongPassages: Critics called the messy first draft the apotheosis of her unfinished career start.
The project’s apotheosis was the day it was cancelled before any work began.
Please apotheosis the window before you leave.

definition: describing a work of visual art in literary form
memoryTip: Ekphrasis = words that re-paint art—a poem about a painting.
correctPassage: Her ekphrastic poem traces each brushstroke of the museum's new landscape.
wrongPassages: His ekphrastic novel never mentioned any painting, sculpture, or photograph.
The lab report was ekphrastic, listing only measurements with no visual subject.
She filed an ekphrastic budget memo that ignored every image in the catalog.

definition: relating to an agent or the capacity to act
memoryTip: Agent-ial: about who can act—having agency.
correctPassage: The theory emphasizes the agential capacity of communities, not only institutions.
wrongPassages: The agential statue sat motionless while visitors walked past it for hours.
Critics called the plot agential because no character ever made a choice.
The agential sample under the microscope showed no motion and no living cells.

definition: the state of being annoyed or worried
correctPassage: Minor technical glitches were a constant source of vexation.
wrongPassages: Her only vexation was the calm joy she felt finishing the puzzle early.
The award speech filled him with pure vexation and lifelong contentment.
Guests described the party as a vexation of laughter, ease, and warm welcome.

definition: words that imitate the sound they name
memoryTip: Buzz, hiss, boom—words that sound like what they mean.
correctPassage: In the comic, every crash panel was filled with bold onomatopoeia.
wrongPassages: The abstract essay relied on onomatopoeia without any sound-imitating words at all.
Her onomatopoeia chapter discussed only silent geometric shapes and color theory.
He labeled pure math symbols as onomatopoeia even though they name no sound.
